doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Art Tatum and Lucky Roberts and day jobs as a way of life
summary: Earlier musicians also held day jobs and played the real music at after-hours sessions.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Yeah. Art Tatum I think worked at the library. He would play his gig. The gig was just a means to the end but the real music would come to the after night sessions. He would go for the sessions. I wasn’t here but this is what I was told. Lucky Roberts played and jammed all night where they would cut heads and that naturally the baddest cat played last and then he would leave and go take a shower or whatever and go and do his regular job during the day at the library or something. So a whole lot of people had day jobs. That was a way of life then.
